blocks.text: Condo buildings in Sumas Prairie

Sumas Prairie is the low agricultural prairie in southeast Abbotsford, in the City of Abbotsford, between Abbotsford and Chilliwack. Plan currency note. Abbotsford's current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025 — the 2016 OCP is not current, and any document citing it as the governing plan is a plan out of date.
Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: Sumas Prairie is an FVREB board sub-area of the City of Abbotsford.

Watershed geography: Sumas Prairie sits in the Sumas River watershed; the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative's six signatories are the Province of B.C., the Semá:th, Máthxwi and Leq'á:mel First Nations, the City of Abbotsford and the City of Chilliwack.
That is a near-empty row: no sales in either split, and no pace or price conclusion can be drawn from it.

Flood — the defining fact of this sub-area: the City hosts the Province's release on the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative, signed in April 2023 in response to widespread flooding on Sumas Prairie from heavy rainfall in November 2021; the Province is providing $3.3 million for critical design and assessment work, and has provided approximately $220 million in recovery, preparedness and mitigation funding for Abbotsford and Sumas Prairie since 2021, including $76.6 million for upgrades to the Barrowtown Pump Station. The same release records that December flooding in the Sumas region again demonstrated the corridor is highly prone to water surges, and that the initiative's studies are at various stages of completion — flood mitigation for the prairie is active planning, not a settled fix.
Health care is outside the sub-area: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Rd, and the Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 2692 Clearbrook Rd #100.

The ALC housing frame on ALR parcels: land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; the principal residence must have a total floor area of 500 m² or less; a secondary suite is permitted in the ALR only within the principal residence; and an additional detached residence may be up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha. ALR status for any specific Sumas Prairie parcel: check parcel by parcel.

The zero is structural, not a slow month. Sumas Prairie's attached row is empty because its land base is farm land under an ALR frame that bars stratification outright — a buyer waiting for a prairie condo project is waiting for a form the governing rules do not produce.

The flood-mitigation money is real, and the plan is still unfinished. Approximately $220 million in provincial funding since 2021 and $76.6 million for the Barrowtown Pump Station sound like a settled fix; the City-hosted release is explicit that the initiative's hydraulic model, risk assessment, ecological assessment and pump-station studies are at various stages of completion, and that December flooding again demonstrated the corridor's exposure. Price the prairie as flood land first, mitigation second.

The sub-area a buyer sees is wider than the prairie floor. Cards labelled "Sumas Prairie" include Majuba Hill and Old Yale Road upland acreage — a hillside house on the fringe carries a different flood and slope profile than a farm parcel on the floor, even though both wear the same sub-area label. Check the individual parcel, not the label.

blocks.text: How a lake became Sumas Prairie

Sumas Prairie was a lake within living memory. Sumas Lake covered roughly 10,000 acres and often tripled in size during the May-to-July freshet; for the Semá:th people of the Stó:lō it was a source of food, a home and a waterway. Settlers farmed around its edge from the 1860s and 1870s, and after a severe flood in 1876 the Province passed a series of dyking and drainage acts, starting with the Sumas Dyking Act of 1878.

The lake was drained under the Sinclair Plan, approved in March 1920. Engineers turned the Vedder River into a canal so it no longer emptied into the lake, built dykes and a dam, and installed pumps at Barrowtown. The first pumps started in July 1923, and by the summer of 1924 the old lake bottom was ready to farm. In 1926 the Canadian Hop Growers Association bought 600 acres of lake bottom and planted what were then the largest hop yards in the Commonwealth; tobacco was grown here too, and two tobacco kilns still stand on the prairie.

A new pumphouse was built between 1980 and 1983, when the Sumas and Vedder dykes were also strengthened. That history is why a farm on the prairie is so productive and why flood protection is the first question to ask about any parcel here: the land sits on a former lake bed kept dry by pumps and dykes.

items.t: This page covers the FVREB "Sumas Prairie" sub-area of the City of Abbotsford.
The board does not publish sub-area medians. (SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)

How people search for it: "Sumas Prairie homes for sale," "Sumas Prairie farms Abbotsford," "Abbotsford acreage Vye Road," and by its farm roads — No. 3 Road, No. 4 Road, Marion Road, Keith Wilson Road.

ALR block (full — this is dyked-prairie farm ground): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified; land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is THREE tiers — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error. ALR status for any specific Sumas Prairie parcel: check parcel by parcel on the ALC maps.
The school on Vye Road is Semá:th Elementary — full stop. Both are rebuild fixes.

The zero attached row is structural, not a slow month. Sumas Prairie's Condos & Townhomes row is 0 / 0 / NA because its land base is farm land under an ALR frame that bars stratification outright, with subdivision minimums of 8.0 ha / 16.0 ha — a buyer waiting for a prairie strata or townhouse project is waiting for a form the governing rules do not produce.

faq.a: Abbotsford's attached stock is in the urban sub-areas.
faq.q: Are there any condos or townhomes in Sumas Prairie?

faq.a: Because ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the housing frame is one principal residence up to 500 m², a suite only inside it, and at most one additional residence of 90 m² (≤40 ha) or 186 m² (>40 ha) — a house on land, never condo lots.
faq.q: Why can't a prairie farmhouse be bought as strata units?

faq.a: Medians are published at community level only (Abbotsford detached $949,000; attached $497,500), not as Sumas Prairie figures.
faq.q: How did Sumas Prairie sell in September 2026?

faq.a: Two locks: ALR residences cannot be stratified.
faq.q: Why can't a prairie farm just be split into townhomes?

faq.a: Where the parcel is in the ALR: one principal residence to 500 m², a suite only within it, and at most one additional detached residence of 90 m² (≤40 ha) or 186 m² (>40 ha).
faq.q: Can I build a second dwelling on a prairie farm parcel?

faq.a: Fee-simple farm parcels and acreages — commercial farm land with barns, country home sites and rural-residential acreages on the prairie floor and its upland fringe, parcel by parcel. There is no named acreage subdivision and no strata land form here at all.
faq.q: What actually trades as acreage on Sumas Prairie?

faq.a: Generally not further: subdivision minimums are 8.0 ha in A1 and 16.0 ha in A2 in the City's parcel-size work, and subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval in any case. Confirm the parcel's zone and ALR status before pricing any split.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a prairie parcel?

faq.a: Two frames sit together: the City's suite cap (under 50% of the principal unit) and coach/garden cap (15% of the lot to a maximum of 100 m²) — Abbotsford's rules only — and, on ALR land, the ALC frame (suite only within the principal residence; additional detached residence capped at 90 m² / 186 m² by parcel size). Confirm the parcel's ALR status and zone first.
faq.q: Can I add a coach house or second dwelling?

faq.a: Get the parcel's elevation, Flood Construction Level position and insurance position in writing before subjects come off.
faq.q: Is flood risk a duplex issue on the prairie?

faq.a: Two SD34 schools, confirmed by name and address against the BC Ministry K-12 file: Semá:th Elementary School at 36321 Vye Rd and Barrowtown Elementary at 5137 Tolmie Rd
